Any fppf covering is an fpqc covering, and a fortiori,
any syntomic, smooth, <ACCENT_0001>tale or Zariski covering is an fpqc covering.

We will show that an fppf covering is an fpqc covering, and then the
rest follows from
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Let <MATH_0001> be an fppf covering.
By definition this means that the <MATH_0002> are flat which checks the first
condition of Definition <REF_0002>. To check the
second, let <MATH_0003> be an affine open subset.
Write <MATH_0004>
for some affine opens <MATH_0005>. Since each <MATH_0006> is open
(Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>), we see that
<MATH_0007>
is an open covering of <MATH_0008>.
Since <MATH_0009> is quasi-compact, this covering has a finite
refinement. This finishes the proof.

<STRUCT_0001>
The fpqc<FOOTNOTEOPEN_0001>The letters fpqc stand for
``fid<ACCENT_0001>lement plat quasi-compacte''.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0001>
topology cannot be treated in the same way as the fppf
topology<FOOTNOTEOPEN_0002>A more precise statement would be that the analogue of
Lemma <REF_0001> for the fpqc topology does not hold.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0002>.
Namely, suppose that <MATH_0001> is a nonzero ring. We will see in
Lemma <REF_0002>
that there does not exist a set <MATH_0002> of fpqc-coverings of <MATH_0003>
such that every fpqc-covering can be refined by an element of <MATH_0004>.
If <MATH_0005> is a field, then the reason for this unboundedness is that
there does not exist a field extension of <MATH_0006> such that every field extension
of <MATH_0007> is contained in it.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
If you ignore set theoretic difficulties, then you run into presheaves
which do not have a sheafification, see
<REF_0003>.
A mildly interesting option is to consider only those faithfully flat ring
extensions <MATH_0008> where the cardinality of <MATH_0009> is suitably bounded.
(And if you consider all schemes in a fixed universe as in SGA4 then you
are bounding the cardinality by a strongly inaccessible cardinal.)
However, it is not so clear what happens if you change the cardinal
to a bigger one.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
For these reasons we do not introduce fpqc sites and we will not consider
cohomology with respect to the fpqc-topology.

<STRUCT_0006><STRUCT_0007>
On the other hand, given a contravariant functor

it does make sense to ask whether <MATH_0011> satisfies the sheaf property
for the fpqc topology, see below.
Moreover, we can wonder about descent of object
in the fpqc topology, etc. Simply put, for certain results the correct
generality is to work with fpqc coverings.
